title: Jeremiah Advises Against Going to Egypt

questions.question: When Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders, along with all the people, approached Jeremiah, what did they ask him to do?
options: "Pray to the Lord your God for us, for all this remnant... that the Lord your God may show us the way we should go, and the thing that we should do."
"Beg the king of Babylon for mercy on our behalf."
"Lead us as military commander against the Chaldeans."
questions.correctAnswer: "Pray to the Lord your God for us, for all this remnant... that the Lord your God may show us the way we should go, and the thing that we should do."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:2-3 (ESV): "Let our plea for mercy come before you, and pray to the Lord your God for us, for all this remnant... that the Lord your God may show us the way we should go, and the thing that we should do."

questions.question: What did the people promise to do regarding the Lord's response?
options: "Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God to whom we are sending you,"
"We will obey only if it aligns with our plans to go to Egypt."
"We will cast lots to see if the message is true."
"We will pay you richly whatever he says."
questions.correctAnswer: "Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God to whom we are sending you,"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:6 (ESV): "Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God to whom we are sending you, that it may be well with us when we obey the voice of the Lord our God."

questions.question: How long did it take for the word of the Lord to come to Jeremiah?
options: At the end of ten days
questions.correctAnswer: At the end of ten days
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:7 (ESV): "At the end of ten days the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah."

questions.question: "If you will remain in this land, then I will build you up and not pull you down; I will plant you, and not pluck you up; for I... of the disaster that I did to you."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:10 (ESV): "for I relent of the disaster that I did to you."

questions.question: The people were afraid of the king of Babylon. What did the Lord say about him?
options: "Do not fear him, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand."
"He will surely return and destroy what is left."
"Flee from him, for he knows what Ishmael did."
"Go to Egypt, for he cannot reach you there."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not fear him, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:11 (ESV): "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid. Do not fear him, declares the Lord, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand."

questions.question: "I will grant you mercy, that he may have mercy on you and let you... in your own land."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:12 (ESV): "I will grant you mercy, that he may have mercy on you and let you remain in your own land."

questions.question: What conditional action did the Lord warn strongly against?
options: "If you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' and so disobey... and if you say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt...'"
"If you rebuild the temple with foreign money..."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' and so disobey... and if you say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt...'"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:13-14 (ESV): "But if you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' and so disobey the voice of the Lord your God, and if you say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt...'"

questions.question: Why did the people say they wanted to go to Egypt?
options: "Where we shall not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread,"
"To find gold and silver in the Nile,"
"Because Pharaoh offered us land in Goshen,"
"To escape the famine that was in Judah,"
questions.correctAnswer: "Where we shall not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread,"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:14 (ESV): "if you say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we shall not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread, and we will dwell there,'"

questions.question: What did the Lord promise would happen to them if they set their faces to go to Egypt?
options: "The sword that you fear shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine of which you are afraid shall follow close after you to Egypt, and there you shall die."
"The Egyptians will make you slaves like your fathers."
"A plague of locusts will consume all you bring."
"The king of Babylon will capture you on the way."
questions.correctAnswer: "The sword that you fear shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine of which you are afraid shall follow close after you to Egypt, and there you shall die."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:16 (ESV): "then the sword that you fear shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine of which you are afraid shall follow close after you to Egypt, and there you shall die."

questions.question: "All the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there shall die by the sword, by famine, and by..."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:17 (ESV): "All the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence."

questions.question: "As my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You shall become an execration, a horror, a... , and a taunt."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:18 (ESV): "You shall become an execration, a horror, a curse, and a taunt. You shall see this place no more."

questions.question: Jeremiah reminded them of their initial hypocritical request: "For you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you... me to the Lord your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the Lord our God... '"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:20 (ESV): "For you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to the Lord your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the Lord our God, and whatever the Lord our God says, declare to us and we will do it.'"

questions.question: "And I have this day declared it to you, but you have not... the voice of the Lord your God in anything that he sent me to tell you."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:21 (ESV): "but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God in anything that he sent me to tell you."

questions.question: "Now therefore know for a certainty that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the... where you desire to go to live."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:22 (ESV): "in the place where you desire to go to live."

questions.question: Why did the people say they were afraid of the Chaldeans in verse 1?
options: Because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land
Because they had stolen Babylonian gold
Because Johanan had refused to pay tribute
Because they wanted to rebel immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 41:18 (Context leading into 42) (ESV): "because of the Chaldeans. For they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land."

key_verse_text: "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid. Do not fear him, declares the Lord, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand."
